subject: Chemistry
title: Bohr's Orbits: Electrons in Shells
description: One-minute skill: Bohr's Orbits: Electrons in Shells.

hook.text: In 1913, Niels Bohr proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels—like planets around a sun.

buildup.text: Classical physics predicted orbiting electrons should radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus. Atoms should collapse.

discovery.text: Bohr said electrons can only exist at certain distances. They jump between levels by absorbing or emitting exact energy.

twist.text: This explained hydrogen's spectral lines perfectly—each color corresponds to an electron jumping between specific levels.

climax.text: Bohr's model was wrong for complex atoms. But it introduced quantization to chemistry—a revolutionary idea.

punchline.text: Fixed orbits, quantum jumps, no spiraling in. A wrong model that changed everything.

quiz.question: What revolutionary idea did Bohr introduce to atomic theory?
options: Electrons exist only in fixed energy levels and jump between them
Electrons orbit randomly at any distance from the nucleus
Electrons are stationary and don't orbit at all

details.summary: In 1913 Niels Bohr proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus only in specific quantized energy levels or shells. Electrons can jump between shells by absorbing or emitting exact amounts of energy, explaining the discrete spectral lines observed in hydrogen's emission spectrum.
details.whyItMatters: Bohr's model introduced quantization into atomic structure, bridging classical physics and quantum mechanics. It explained hydrogen's spectrum precisely and inspired the quantum revolution.
takeaways: Electrons occupy fixed energy shells around the nucleus
Jumps between shells absorb or emit specific photon energies
The model perfectly predicted hydrogen's spectral lines

faq.question: Why does the Bohr model work well for hydrogen but not larger atoms?
faq.answer: Hydrogen has only one electron, making its interactions simple enough for Bohr's circular orbit math. Multi-electron atoms involve electron-electron repulsions and complex orbital shapes that require the full Schrödinger equation and quantum mechanical orbitals to describe accurately.

faq.question: What did Bohr mean by quantized energy levels?
faq.answer: Quantized means only specific discrete energy values are allowed, not a continuous range. Electrons cannot exist between shells. They must absorb exactly the right energy to jump up or release exactly the right energy to drop down, producing specific colors of light.
